Title: NST Leader: Malaysia cannot arrest its way out of the drug menace
Article:
The
Crime Statistics, Malaysia, 2026
report, released by the Statistics Department, makes for uncomfortable reading. The figure that stands out is the 152,856 positive urine tests  recorded for controlled drugs and other psychoactive substances in 2025.
This is a stark reminder that the fight against drug abuse in the country is far from won.
Although the figure represents a 2.6 per cent decline from the 157,014 cases recorded in 2024, the decrease is marginal, with the overall number remaining alarmingly high.
There is little room for comfort, much less complacency. Efforts to combat drug abuse must be intensified.
The stubbornly high numbers ought to prompt a deeper question: are we doing enough to tackle the problem at its roots, or are we too focused on enforcement, effectively closing  the gate after the horse has bolted? The problem highlights the limits of relying too heavily on enforcement.
To be sure,  police must continue to target drug syndicates, traffickers and suppliers.
But arrests and seizures alone cannot solve the problem if demand for drugs remains high, whether for recreational use or among those  addicted, and new users continue to emerge.
Prevention must begin early. Schools, families and communities all have a role to play in educating young people about the dangers of drug abuse. Awareness campaigns must be sustained and meaningful, rather than mere token exercises. Rehabilitation is equally important.
Addiction cannot be addressed through shame and punishment alone. Effective responses must include treatment, counselling and reintegration into society.
Greater emphasis must be placed on preventing relapse and helping people in recovery rebuild their lives.
The value of second chances must also be recognised. A holistic approach must also address the root causes of drug abuse.
The authorities must seek to understand why people turn to drugs, identify vulnerable groups and strengthen cooperation among enforcement agencies, healthcare providers and community organisations.
We must also seek new ways to measure success in tackling the menace. Positive outcomes matter more than the number of arrests.
The true measure of success lies in whether anti-drug efforts are producing lasting results.
Do they lead to measurable and widespread reductions in drug abuse, fewer repeat offences and lower rates of relapse among people recovering from addiction? Recent high-profile cross-border drug-smuggling cases are also cause for concern.
They raise questions about whether our enforcement agencies are keeping pace with the changing tactics of trafficking syndicates.
Malaysia appears to face a significant drug-abuse problem, but how does it compare with its regional neighbours when population size is taken into account? Could our location in the heart of Southeast Asia also make the nation a convenient transit point for illicit drug trafficking? We must not let down our guard in this fight.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hamzah: Wawasan wants to defend seats won under PN in Melaka
Article:
JASIN: Perikatan Nasional (PN) wants to defend the seats it won in the previous Melaka election, said Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
He said if Umno wanted to defend the seats it had won, the same principle should apply to Wawasan.
"Both state seats held by the former opposition assemblymen in Melaka are now represented by Wawasan members.
"If Umno says it wants to defend the seats it won, why should I not be allowed to defend the seats we won?" he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after chairing Wawasan's supreme council meeting at Heritage Hotel here today. Also present was the party's secretary-general, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah.
Hamzah, who is also Larut member of parliament, said Wawasan was open to discussing seat swaps if Barisan Nasional (BN) had seats it wanted the party to contest.
"If they want a particular seat, that is possible, but I have made it clear that we want to defend our seats.
"If they want to negotiate, they must sit down with us to discuss suitable seats — seats that could determine victory for either PN or BN," he said.
Commenting on speculation that Wawasan would contest only one state seat in Melaka, Paya Rumput, Hamzah described it as speculation but did not confirm the number of seats the party would contest.
He said a decision on Wawasan's participation in the Melaka election would be announced after the court delivers its decision on Oct 22.
Earlier, media reports suggested that Wawasan was almost certain to be allocated Paya Rumput, with the party's Tangga Batu division pro-tem chief, Ramlan Meon, 40, tipped as a potential candidate.
The reports said the development could affect the chances of former assemblymen Dr Mohd Aleef Yusof and Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub, who won Sungai Udang and Bemban respectively under the PN ticket in the 2021 Melaka election before leaving Bersatu to join Wawasan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sisi says Egypt ready to defend Saudi Arabia 'if requested'
Article:
CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that Egypt was ready to defend Saudi Arabia "if requested", as fighting flares between the kingdom and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
Since Yemen's war reignited in July, the Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.
The Houthis have also blockaded the Bab al-Mandab Strait, piling pressure on energy exports as Iran presses its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz.
Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy, Sisi said Egypt was "not looking for a role to play" in regional conflicts, but added that it was "inconceivable" for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was "harmed or its security and stability threatened".
"Egypt, of course, with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will carry out any measure to protect you or defend you," he said.
He added that any deployment would require parliamentary approval and said he hoped lawmakers would convene in an emergency session to grant authorisation "if it is requested of us".
"I'm not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone," Sisi said. "We are speaking only about defence."
During a visit to Egypt last month, de facto Saudi leader Mohammed bin Salman and Sisi called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea, a vital trade route.
The conflict with the Houthis poses risks not only to Saudi Arabia's security and energy exports, but also to Egypt, where disruption to Red Sea shipping could further reduce revenues from the Suez Canal, a key source of foreign currency.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last month that the Suez Canal had lost about US$11 billion in revenue since the Houthis began attacking commercial vessels following Hamas's Oct 7, 2023, attack on Israel.
Despite its longstanding military ties with Gulf states, Egypt has not joined the Mecca agreement, a mutual defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan in August, with Cairo generally favouring diplomacy over participation in regional military alliances.
Saudi Arabia has long been a key backer of Egypt, providing financial support after the 2013 ouster of the late Islamist president Mohamed Morsi and during subsequent economic crises.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police debunk claims of Bangladeshis gathering in Bukit Bintang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities have dismissed claims that Bangladeshis recently gathered in Bukit Bintang.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks found that the original video showed New Year celebrations in Bukit Bintang in 2022 and had been edited using artificial intelligence (AI).
"The video is old footage showing the Selangor Foundation Building, which is old and worn. The issue being chanted about in the video was the Comilla issue in Bangladesh in 2022," he said in a statement.
Fadil also said no gatherings involving Bangladeshi citizens or any other groups had been recorded in Bukit Bintang from January to October this year.
A short video circulated on social media over the past few days, claiming that a group of Bangladeshis had gathered in the capital to demand self-administrative powers for the Comilla region. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman arrested over baby's body found in Terengganu drain
Article:
KUALA BERANG: Police have arrested a 23-year-old woman to assist in investigations into the discovery of a baby's body in a drain at the Padang Setengge residential area here yesterday.
Hulu Terengganu police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said the woman was arrested at her residence at 3.30pm for investigation under Section 318 of the Penal Code.
He said the arrest enabled police to establish the circumstances surrounding the birth and the woman's involvement in the incident.
"The post-mortem conducted by a pathologist from the Forensic Department of Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) this morning found that the baby was full-term and had died more than 24 hours before the examination at 9am.
"However, it could not be determined whether the baby was born alive or dead, nor could the cause of death be ascertained. The sex of the baby has also not been determined," he said in a statement today.
It was reported yesterday that a
woman discovered the baby's body
, with several limbs missing, in a drain while washing clothes behind her house in the Padang Setengge residential area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman arrested after baby’s body found in Kuala Berang drain missing head, hand; gender unknown
Article:
KUALA BERANG, Oct 18 — Police have arrested a local woman to assist in investigations into the discovery of a baby’s body in a drain at the Padang Setengge residential area near here on Friday afternoon.
Hulu Terengganu police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said the 23-year-old suspect was arrested at her residence at 3.30pm for investigation under Section 318 of the Penal Code.
He said the arrest enabled police to establish the circumstances surrounding the birth and the suspect’s involvement in the incident, bringing the investigation to a close within 24 hours.
“The post-mortem conducted by a pathologist from the Forensic Department of Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) this morning found that the baby was full-term and had died more than 24 hours before the examination at 9am.
“However, it could not be determined whether the baby was born alive or dead, nor could the cause of death be ascertained. The sex of the baby has also not been determined,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Bernama reported yesterday that a woman discovered the body of a baby with several missing limbs in a drain while washing clothes behind her house in the Padang Setengge residential area. — Bernama

Title: Three-year-old boy dies after fall from 11th floor in Sepang
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 18 — Police have confirmed that a young boy, aged around three, died after falling from the 11th floor of a residential building in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi here, yesterday morning.
Sepang district police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said his team received a report regarding the incident at 5.54am today.
“The victim, a Malay boy, was confirmed dead at the scene,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Norhizam said the investigation paper was opened under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001.
The post-mortem process on the victim at the Sultan Idris Shah Hospital, Serdang, has also been completed, he said.
In this regard, Norhizam advised the public not to spread unverified information regarding the incident.
“Individuals with information related to the incident are requested to contact the investigating officer, Inspector Mohamad Farizi Ramlee, at 014-314 5347,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Five held after luxury home in Iskandar Puteri allegedly used to scam Singaporeans
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 18 — A luxury house in Iskandar Puteri allegedly used as a call centre to lure Singaporeans into fake investments has been raided, with five suspects arrested.
The syndicate allegedly promised returns of between 100 and 300 per cent, with senior citizens believed to make up most of its victims,
The Star
reported today.
“The foreigners, a Chinese national and an Indonesian, were women,” a police official was quoted as saying, without being named.
The five suspects, aged between 18 and 41, comprised three Malaysians and two foreigners, and were recruited through social media with promises of monthly salaries of about RM3,000 as customer relations officers, the report said.
Police seized electronic devices worth more than RM100,000, while investigations continue.
Johor recorded 9,897 scam investigation papers involving RM212.6 million in losses between January and September this year, with an average of 37 scam reports filed daily, state police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said.
Malaysian Community Crime Care Pahang branch chairman Daniel Khoo called for tougher action against syndicate members, arguing that fines under the Passport Act were insufficient and that foreign offenders should be deported and barred from re-entering Malaysia.

Title: Man, 52, found dead in drain near Taman Ciku in Bukit Mertajam
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 18 — The body of a 52-year-old man was found in a drain near Taman Ciku here yesterday.
The discovery was reported to the authorities at about 4.30pm, prompting firefighters to head to the scene to recover the body,
The New Straits Times
reported.
Preliminary investigations indicated that the man died less than 24 hours before he was found.
His body was taken to Bukit Mertajam Hospital for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.
Police are investigating the case.

Title: Haze: Schools, educational institutions in Johor to close for another five days from tomorrow
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 18 — The Johor government has extended the closure of schools and educational institutions across the state for another five days from tomorrow (October 19) due to the haze.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following a meeting of the Johor Haze Management Coordination Committee at noon yesterday.
He said the extension would remain subject to developments in air quality, weather forecasts and ongoing health assessments.
“Monitoring reports indicate that Air Pollutant Index (API) readings remain at concerning levels, with no significant improvement.
“The decision also takes into account wind movement towards the north and weather forecasts for the next three to four days, which will be considered before determining when schools can reopen,” he said in a statement.
Muhammad Naqib said the measure was in line with the directive of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, who consistently prioritised the safety, health and well-being of the people.
He said the decision also reflected the state government’s commitment to placing public health and safety at the forefront.
Meanwhile, he said Teaching and Learning at Home (PdPR) would continue throughout the closure in accordance with the Ministry of Education’s (MOE) PdPR Manual Version 2.0.
However, the needs of students sitting for examinations and assessments would be taken into account, with limited exceptions possible.
“These exceptions are subject to coordination by the Johor Education Department (JPNJ) and strict compliance with health standard operating procedures (SOPs), with no additional activities permitted,” he said.
Muhammad Naqib said JPNJ would review the implementation SOPs daily in line with MOE directives and obtain the latest updates from the Examination Board to coordinate examination and assessment schedules for MOE schools and Johor religious schools.
He stressed that face masks must be worn and all established health guidelines followed.
Regarding private educational institutions (IPS) and childcare centres, Muhammad Naqib said the decision on whether to continue operating or close rested with the respective institutions.
“However, this is subject to compliance with the established guidelines, including conducting activities in enclosed spaces and ensuring that face masks are worn,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said health authorities had raised concerns over the public health risks of prolonged exposure to air pollution and recommended more comprehensive preventive measures, particularly for children and vulnerable groups.
“Throughout October, 30,648 cases of asthma and upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) were recorded in the state, representing a weekly increase of 20.7 per cent,” he said.
The state government had earlier announced the closure of all schools for two days from October 8, before extending the closure to cover educational institutions for another five days from October 12. — Bernama

Title: Boy dies after running onto road to retrieve ball in Terengganu
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 17 — An eight-year-old boy was killed after being struck by a lorry while retrieving a ball that had rolled onto the road in Kampung Surau Haji Daud here this afternoon.
Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said police received a report from a member of the public at 4.10pm about an accident involving a lorry and a pedestrian.
“Preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred at about 3.40pm when the lorry driver, travelling from Kampung Surau Haji Daud, struck the victim, who had suddenly run onto the road to retrieve a ball that had rolled onto it.
“The victim died at the scene from severe injuries to various parts of his body,” he said in a statement today.
Azli said the victim, a pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan Kubang Ikan, had been taken to the Forensic Department of Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital for a post-mortem examination.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: The abbreviation ACP stands for Assistant Commissioner of Police.

Title: Civil Defence Force to run emergency control centres round the clock for monsoon season
Article:
KLUANG, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) is strengthening its preparedness for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL) by operating its operations control centres around the clock to coordinate emergency responses and disaster relief.
APM Deputy Chief Commissioner (Operations) Ghazali Abd Rahman said the move was backed by improved communication systems and closer coordination with agencies on disaster management committees at various levels to address the risks of floods, water surges and landslides.
He said communication between the southern, eastern and central zones would be improved to ensure effective coordination and allow personnel from other zones to be deployed to disaster-hit areas.
“Effective communication between zones will enable additional members to be deployed to support the more than 12,000 personnel on standby for the 2026/2027 MTL.
“We will mobilise support teams from the respective zones and work together across zones to conduct exercises and assist one another during disasters,” he said.
He was speaking after the closing ceremony of the 2026 APM Strategic Partnership Programme with the Media for the Southern Zone at the Southern Region Civil Defence Training Centre here today.
Ghazali said APM was also stepping up preparedness by improving personnel skills, maintaining and expanding its assets and logistics to ensure smooth rescue operations throughout the monsoon season.
He also welcomed the increase in allowances for APM volunteers announced in Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, with rates for personnel rising from RM8 to RM9 and those for officers from RM9.80 to RM10.80.
“Although the increase may seem small, it will boost morale and encourage personnel to provide the best possible service to the public and the country,” he said. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: The abbreviation APM in Malay stands for Angkatan Pertahanan Awam Malaysia, or the Malaysian Civil Defence Force. MTL stands for Monsun Timur Laut, or the Northeast Monsoon.

Title: After another downpour, Lembah Subang resident asks minister to step in over recurring floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Flash floods hit several parts of the Klang Valley after heavy rain this afternoon, as a Lembah Subang resident raised concerns over recurring floods in the neighbourhood, alleging that an unfinished pedestrian walkway project may be obstructing nearby drains.
Flooding was reported in several areas, including USJ 1, USJ 7, Sunway, Ara Damansara, Kota Damansara, Kampung Baru Hicom and Shah Alam, with inundated roads disrupting traffic.
“Can the minister look into the problems faced by residents here, who have to deal with flooding in our neighbourhood every time it rains?” Threads user _anuarlatif said in a post today.
The user alleged that soil and construction materials left beside the main road in Taman Putra Damai, Lembah Subang, had entered nearby drains, blocking the flow of water during rain.
The user also claimed that work on the pedestrian walkway had remained unfinished for a long time, blaming the contractor for the recurring problem.
“When it rains, soil and materials fall into the drains, eventually blocking them,” the user said.
Threads user _anuarlatif highlighted the recurrent flooding in his Lembah Subang neighborhood after a heavy downpour on October 17, 2026, which he believes is caused by leftover construction material flowing into the drains and causing blockage. — Threads screenshots
Petaling Jaya City Council acknowledged the complaint and asked the user to provide the full address of the affected location so it could check the site and determine what further action was needed.
“Please provide the full address of the affected location to facilitate checks and further action by the council,” the council said.
Another Threads user, amm.yusopp, also reported flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang.
The alleged link between the unfinished walkway and the recurring floods has not been independently verified, while details on the extent of flooding at the two neighbourhoods and its impact on residents were not immediately available.

Title: Missing father and son found weak after three days in Terengganu forest without food
Article:
JERTIH, Oct 17 — A father and son who went missing on Thursday while searching for medicinal roots in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut were found safe at noon today.
Adam Adnan, 25, and his father Adnan Mohamad, 57, were found by a search and rescue (SAR) team at 12.40pm, about three kilometres from the operation’s command post.
Besut police chief Supt Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said the two were brought out of the forest at 2.45pm via the Lata Kolam Air Deru recreational area.
“The two men were found weak after going without food for three days while lost in the forest.
“They were assisted down by the rescue team before being taken by a Civil Defence Force (APM) ambulance to Besut Hospital for further treatment,” he told reporters here today.
Bernama reported earlier today that the father and son had gone missing after entering the forest to search for medicinal roots. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Islamic affairs gets RM3.1b, as minister outlines support for ‘pondok’ schools, imams and halal SMEs
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — The Madani Government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under Budget 2027 to strengthen Islamic development, including support for religious education institutions and the welfare of religious personnel nationwide.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said 85.4 per cent of the allocation was for operating expenditure, while the remaining 14.6 per cent was set aside for development expenditure.
He said the increase reflected the government’s commitment to a more comprehensive agenda to elevate the stature of Islam and benefit society.
“The Madani Government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for
sekolah agama rakyat
(community religious schools),
tahfiz
institutions and
sekolah pondok
(traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
“The scope of assistance has also been expanded to cover the operating costs of these institutions,” he said in a statement here today.
Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including
Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain
(Kafa) teachers,
takmir
teachers, imams, bilals,
tok siaks
,
nojas
and
marbuts
, in recognition of their contributions to the community.
He said 500 Kafa teachers who taught students with special needs, including those who used sign language or the Braille Quran, would receive a special monthly incentive of RM150.
“The well-being of those who enliven the Houses of Allah is further supported by a special government allocation that fully covers Social Security Organisation contributions for 40,000 imams, bilals,
tok siaks
, mosque staff and
takmir
teachers.
“The Pilgrims Fund Board (Tabung Haji) serves as the implementing agency, ensuring continuous social security protection and providing peace of mind to these individuals as they serve the ummah,” he said.
In a related development, Zulkifli said amendments to the Road Transport Act requiring drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their families contained elements consistent with the Islamic legal concept of diyat, or financial compensation.
He said the concept recognised the right of victims or their heirs to receive compensation for harm caused by another person’s actions.
Zulkifli said the government was also strengthening the halal industry by offering matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.
A separate grant of RM25,000 would be available to empower halal-certified MSMEs in high-potential sectors, including cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, he added.
In the Islamic education sector, he said Jakim and the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) had initiated a collaboration to provide digital devices and skills training to teachers and students at more than 300
pondok
schools nationwide.
Zulkifli said the initiatives reflected the government’s approach of focusing not only on economic and infrastructure development but also on nurturing a knowledgeable, ethical and prosperous society.
“This Budget 2027 framework is formulated based on a philosophy that aspires to reach for the skies while remaining firmly rooted on the ground.
“We aim to elevate the nation’s economy and the stature of Islam to the pinnacle of success, guided by a far-sighted vision,” he said.
He added that the government’s priorities and policy implementation would remain grounded in reality, with the ultimate aim of safeguarding the welfare and well-being of Malaysians. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Jakim is the abbreviation for Jabatan Kemajuan Islam Malaysia in Malay, or the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia in English.
Tahfiz
refers to the memorisation of the Quran and, in this context, institutions dedicated to teaching it.
Takmir
refers to religious classes or activities organised to enliven and strengthen mosque life.
Kafa
stands for Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain, or Quran and Fardu Ain classes that teach children Quran recitation and memorisation, as well as basic Islamic religious obligations and practices.
Bilal
refers to a mosque official who assists the imam and calls Muslims to prayer.
Tok siak
refers to a mosque caretaker or attendant.
Noja
(plural: nojas) refers to a person responsible for maintaining a mosque and assisting with its daily operations.
Marbut
refers to a mosque caretaker or person responsible for its upkeep.

Title: Selangor Islamic council denies Jais ‘frame-up’ claims in Nik Nazmi’s khalwat detention, says no one is above the law
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) has denied allegations that the detention of former Setiawangsa MP Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) last Thursday over a khalwat case was an act of persecution or a “frame-up”.
Mais chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said Jais had acted on an official complaint and followed established legal procedures, without manipulating the situation to target any individual.
“The suggestion that the religious department was involved in manipulation or anything of the sort is entirely untrue.
“We have a legal obligation... when a complaint is lodged, we are required to conduct a thorough investigation.
“Rest assured, Jais will carry out the investigation as diligently as possible, and if there is clear evidence, we will proceed with charges in court,” he said.
He told reporters this after the 2026 Gathering of Accredited Religious Teachers in Selangor at the Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Silver Jubilee Hall here today, which was also attended by Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir.
Salehuddin said the case was made public to clarify that Syariah laws were enforced fairly, regardless of the background or influence of the individual under investigation.
He urged the public to give Jais sufficient time and space to complete its investigation and refrain from speculation that could compromise the fairness of the legal process.
“We cannot pass judgment while the investigation is still incomplete.
“We must act fairly and carry out our duties in accordance with the regulations.
“If we were to act outside these regulations, we ourselves would be subject to accusations,” he said.
Earlier, Nik Nazmi confirmed in a statement on his Instagram account that he was one of two individuals detained by Jais in Petaling Jaya last Thursday over allegations of khalwat, and said he was prepared to cooperate with any legal proceedings.
On a separate case involving a local youth suspected of participating in the rituals of another religion, Salehuddin said preliminary findings suggested that the individual’s actions were, so far, a matter of personal belief.
However, he said Jais was examining various forms of digital evidence, including social media posts concerning rituals at Batu Caves that had been linked to other belief systems.
“The public must understand that when we intend to take legal action in court, we must ensure that all evidence is authentic.
“We are aware that material could potentially be superimposed or generated via AI (artificial intelligence); therefore, we have experts who can verify its authenticity.
“Regarding the issue of apostasy, we cannot impose penalties without conducting a thorough investigation.
“We certainly consult with the relevant authorities before taking action against anyone.
“A comprehensive investigation must be carried out first,” he said.
On October 13, Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said a man who went viral over allegations that he had performed rituals of another religion in breach of Syariah law had been detained alongside his mother in Kuala Lumpur to assist in an investigation under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The acronym Mais in Malay stands for Majlis Agama Islam Selangor, or the Selangor Islamic Religious Council. Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, or the Selangor Islamic Religious Department.

Title: Stop dumping pet fish in lakes, govt warns as alien species wiping out natives in Ampang lake
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Alien fish account for 95 per cent of fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir, posing a serious threat to the balance of Malaysia’s freshwater ecosystem.
Agriculture and Food Security Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak said mitigation efforts needed to be strengthened through data-driven approaches, community education and strategic cooperation involving the government, private sector and non-governmental organisations.
He warned that releasing pet fish into lakes, dams and public waterways when they grow too large or become difficult to care for could harm aquatic biodiversity and threaten the survival of local species.
“If we do not educate, this matter will become a culture that is difficult to curb and will become a long-term problem,” he said at the “Program Kelestarian Perikanan Darat: Mitigasi Memburu Ikan Asing” at Tasik Ampang Hilir here today.
The alien fish-catching programme, conducted from 2022 to 2025, recorded a total catch of 19.74 tonnes, highlighting the need to address the spread of these species more seriously.
Isham said measures included increasing efforts to catch alien fish, releasing local fish fry to help restore the balance of fish populations and expanding public education to discourage people from releasing pet fish into public waters.
He said the ministry was also reviewing ways to tighten existing regulations, including the possibility of banning certain fish species identified as threats to local ecosystems.
Agrobank released 1,400 native fish fry into the lake to support the conservation of local species, comprising 1,100 baung and 300 lampam sungai.
Records from the Malaysian Department of Fisheries showed that 146 of the 154 fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir were alien species, while only eight were native species.
Agrobank chief development officer Ahmad Arif Abu Bakar said efforts to restore the balance between native and alien fish populations needed to be supported by greater public awareness and education on the importance of protecting Malaysia’s biodiversity.
“The public needs to understand their responsibility in maintaining the ecosystem, including not releasing pet fish into rivers or lakes when the fish grow larger,” he said.
The programme brought together about 250 participants from seven agencies and organisations, with activities including catching alien fish using seine nets, cast nets, fishing lines and fish traps. — Bernama

Title: Penang’s RM420m link road to Silicon Island targets first bridge opening by 2028
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — A total of 202.3 hectares of land have been reclaimed at Silicon Island since reclamation works began in September 2023, marking progress in the development of Penang’s next economic growth hub as of October 2026.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the development was envisioned to complement the state’s semiconductor industry while attracting investments in advanced technology, research and development, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven innovation.
“The early launch of the Silicon Island Experience Centre offers visitors a closer look at our vision for a new growth hub that will complement Penang’s semiconductor industry and attract investments in advanced technology, research and development, and AI-driven innovation,” he said in a Facebook post today.
He said Silicon Island was also expected to create quality jobs, develop local talent and benefit surrounding communities, with sustainability remaining a key priority.
Chow said the state government hoped that, with the right support and strategic partnerships, it could take Penang’s economy to the next level and build a stronger, greener future for generations to come.
In a separate statement, Silicon Island Development Sdn Bhd said the Silicon Island Experience Centre was now open to government agencies, investors, local communities and strategic partners to help them better understand the 931-hectare development.
It said the 2,500-square-foot facility featured an interactive LED scale model showcasing key components of the development, including a 283-hectare Green Tech Park, commercial precincts, transit corridors and more than 110 kilometres of dedicated cycling and pedestrian paths.
Built at a cost of RM2.5 million, the centre was completed in four months.
Silicon Island is designed as a smart city with a five-diamond Low Carbon City accreditation, with its development expected to support Penang’s long-term economic growth while incorporating sustainable urban planning.
Penang Infrastructure Corporation Sdn Bhd chief executive officer and Silicon Island Development chairman Datuk Seri Farizan Darus said reclamation works began in September 2023, with 202.3 hectares of land physically reclaimed as of October 2026.
“Physical progress on the RM420 million Pan Island Link 2A contract is also moving smoothly.
“We are targeting the opening of the first section of the marine bridge connecting Jalan Permatang Damar Laut directly to Silicon Island by December 2028, leading towards full completion by June 2029,” he said. — Bernama

Title: From USJ to Shah Alam, flash floods disrupt Klang Valley roads after afternoon downpour
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Afternoon thunderstorms brought flash floods to several parts of the Klang Valley today, inundating roads and disrupting traffic in Selangor as authorities urged motorists to avoid affected areas.
Social media posts reported flooding in USJ 1, USJ 7, Sunway, Ara Damansara, Kota Damansara, Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Baru Hicom and Shah Alam, with motorists warned to plan their journeys carefully.
In Shah Alam, the city council warned of rising water levels near the traffic lights at i-City in Section 7 and Padang Jawa in Section 16, advising the public to drive cautiously and avoid affected roads if water levels continued to rise.
The Malaysian Highway Authority also reported flash floods at Ramp C of the Guthrie Corridor Expressway interchange from Shah Alam towards Bukit Jelutong at 5.40pm, with the left lane blocked and only the right lane passable, although traffic was reported to be under control.
The flooding followed an earlier warning from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several parts of the country, including Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat in Selangor.
The weather warning also covered areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Terengganu, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan, Johor and Sarawak, with the forecast conditions expected until 3pm.
On social media, a user warned motorists in USJ to plan their routes, saying: “For those in USJ, plan your route — flooding and traffic jams.”
Another Facebooker reported falling into a drain during flooding in Sunway, writing: “Sunway was flooded earlier, then I fell into a drain and got soaked.”
The Shah Alam City Council advised the public to monitor updates through its i-LenSA portal at ilensa.mbsa.gov.my or contact its 24-hour Pantas hotline at 03-5510 5811.
Motorists were urged to remain alert, avoid driving through floodwaters and check road conditions before setting out.

Title: GRS takes its election pitch to Kudat, with Hajiji eyeing 16 parliamentary seats
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor is scheduled to address more than 3,000 delegates and observers at the 2026 GRS Convention in Kudat tomorrow (Sunday), which aims to prepare the coalition to win at least 16 of the 26 parliamentary seats.
“Although GRS was returned to power in the State election in November last year, the convention also serves to remind that GRS should not rest on its laurels but continue to work hard towards the betterment of the State and people.
“Cooperation and unity among GRS components as well as our partners in the State Unity Government is vital to ensure a decisive victory for GRS in the coming general election,” said Hajiji, who is GRS Chairman and PGRS President.
The inaugural convention in Kudat will be held at Dewan Tun Mustapha, with participants and observers representing all 26 parliamentary constituencies in Sabah, including Labuan.Hajiji said the venue follows a decision by the GRS Supreme Council that the convention should be rotated among the various districts instead of being centred solely in Kota Kinabalu.
Besides Hajiji’s keynote address, the six GRS Deputy Chairmen will deliver speeches. They represent the core leadership of the six GRS component parties, namely PGRS, PBS, PCS, LDP, PHRS and Upko.
Hajiji said the convention will bring together central leadership and key divisional leaders for discussions and sharing sessions with two focuses.
The first is political strategy to strengthen party preparedness, particularly ahead of the 16th General Election.
The second is an assessment of progress on the development agenda for the people and the State under the GRS Manifesto, specifically by advancing the Hala Tuju Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) 2.0 roadmap.
He said GRS’ partners in the State Government are also expected to perform well and deliver more seats so that Sabah’s voice can be heard in Parliament.
Hajiji added that the political dynamics in Sabah favour GRS and the coalition will enter the general election with full confidence of gaining the trust of voters.
The choice of Kudat is seen by many as a sign of GRS’ confidence in capturing the Kota Marudu and Kudat parliamentary seats, which are held by Parti KDM and an Independent respectively. Both Members of Parliament lost in the State election in November last year to GRS candidates.­ — Daily Express
* Editor’s note: GRS stands for Gabungan Rakyat Sabah; PGRS stands for Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah; PBS stands for Parti Bersatu Sabah; PCS stands for Parti Cinta Sabah; LDP stands for Liberal Democratic Party; PHRS stands for Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah; Upko stands for United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation; and SMJ stands for Sabah Maju Jaya.

Title: Sarawak polls could be as early as November, says state minister Abdul Karim
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — Sarawak could hold its 13th state election as early as November, with the polling window extending to mid-December, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
“The window is getting smaller. I would say we only have about one and a half months — November and half of December,” he told reporters at an event here.
Abdul Karim, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief, said the timing would depend on when Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg dissolves the Sarawak Legislative Assembly.
The Election Commission (EC) would then determine the polling date in accordance with the law, he said.
He added that the election timetable must allow sufficient time for the EC to prepare and for campaigning to take place.
A state election must be held within 60 days of the Assembly’s dissolution, a deadline that also applies if its term expires automatically. — Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: The abbreviation DUN in Malay stands for Dewan Undangan Negeri, or State Legislative Assembly.

Title: Melaka polls: PKR to field experienced, young and women candidates, says Amirudin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to firm up its direction for the Melaka state election within a week, with candidate selection now in its final stages, coalition election strategy director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today.
He said the coalition wanted to field candidates with a record of serving the community and relevant experience, while giving newcomers opportunities in some constituencies where its traditional support was weaker.
“In some state constituencies where our support is relatively low, we will allow candidates to gain experience. This is part of the party’s and Pakatan Harapan’s long-term plan,” he told reporters after attending the Semarak Kasih event with Yayasan Selangor students here, national news wire
Bernama
reported.
Amirudin said allowing candidates to gain experience in less favourable constituencies could help build a longer-term plan for PKR and the wider coalition.
He also touched on possible cooperation with Bersatu, saying the matter had not been finalised and a decision would be made soon.
PKR has previously confirmed that it will contest nine seats in the Melaka election.
Party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said Pakatan Harapan would contest more seats overall if PKR’s allocation remained at nine.
PH is scheduled to announce its candidate on October 24.
The Melaka state election has been set for November 14 with nominations on October 31 and early voting on November 10.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional two.

Title: Home minister: 24-hour border watch, jetty demolitions to curb cross-border crime in Kelantan
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — Police are maintaining round-the-clock surveillance along all border routes in Kelantan to curb cross-border crime, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the directive had been issued to Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat to ensure continuous physical surveillance along the border.
“Among the measures taken are the demolition of illegal jetties and enforcement of the law against individuals crossing the border without valid documents,” he told a press conference after attending the launch ceremony for the 2026 Home Ministry’s Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives here today.
However, he said enforcement measures might not completely eliminate cross-border crime, as it involves organised criminal networks that had been operating for a long time.
Therefore, Saifuddin Nasution said efforts to curb such activities required the cooperation of all parties and could not rely solely on the Home Ministry and the police.
Meanwhile, when asked to comment on the case involving an incident concerning Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, he said police were completing several aspects of the investigation papers after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) requested improvements before a further decision could be made.
Saifuddin Nasution said the investigation papers had been submitted to the AGC within a week of the incident.
He said the AGC subsequently asked police to complete several aspects of the investigation to ensure that the information and evidence gathered were sufficient for further consideration.
He said the investigation papers included witness statements and information gathered throughout the investigation.
The AGC could return the investigation papers to police for further completion if additional information was required before a decision was made, he added.
Previously, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was reported as saying that the investigation was being conducted by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which deals with voluntarily causing hurt to another person.
Mohd Khalid said statements had been recorded from 25 witnesses so far to assist in the investigation into the incident, which occurred on September 28.
The media had earlier reported that Mohd Shuhaily had left it to the government to decide on any action that might be taken against him following a viral video showing him reprimanding an individual at KLIA Terminal 1.
Mohd Shuhaily said the matter had been brought to the attention of the country’s top leadership and the Home Ministry, and that he was prepared to accept any decision on the issue. — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry: Over 6,700 officers approved for promotions and acting appointments, including four chopper crash victims
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — A total of 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the Ministry of Health (MOH) have been approved for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15.
The approvals were granted by the Public Service Promotion Board (LKPPA) on October 13, according to a statement issued today.
The move reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to recognise officers’ commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery.
In line with improvements to career progression under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), the board also approved excellence-based promotion criteria for officers under MOH’s teaching service scheme, allowing them to be promoted without a vacant post.
The approval provides the officers concerned with better opportunities for career advancement.
The ministry also paid tribute to four officers who served with the Flying Doctor Service (PDU) and died in a helicopter crash while on duty on September 8.
All four were approved for posthumous promotions in recognition of their service and dedication.
The ministry expressed confidence that such recognition would encourage continued excellence and strengthen officers’ commitment to building a high-quality, sustainable and responsive national healthcare system.
It will continue to review and implement improvements to ensure officers’ welfare and career development receive due attention. — Bernama

Title: ‘That is not our job’: Amirudin rejects claims PKR plotted khalwat trap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari today denied allegations that the party orchestrated a khalwat case involving former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad to undermine a political rival.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said PKR had never discussed or arranged any plan, privately or publicly, to entrap political opponents, news outlet Harian Metro reported.
“We have many other things to do than arrange khalwat cases.
“That is not our job,” he told reporters after launching the Semarak Kasih Yayasan Selangor 2026 programme today.
He added that the party did not want personal matters to become the basis of political rivalry or debate.
Khalwat is an offence under Islamic law involving a Muslim man and woman who are not married to each other being found alone together in circumstances that may suggest improper conduct.
The allegations surfaced after the Selangor Islamic Religious Department detained two people in Petaling Jaya last Thursday to assist investigations into a suspected khalwat offence.
The department confirmed yesterday that a man and a woman had been detained at about 6pm in Petaling Jaya under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995, but did name the people involved.
Nik Nazmi, a PKR member for almost 21 years till his exit in May, confirmed publicly earlier today that he was one of two people detained and apologised to his wife, family and his current party over what he described as a lapse in judgement.
Parti Bersama Malaysia has since announced that its 44-year-old co-founder is to be suspended three months from October 20 following the khalwat scandal.

Title: KL Immigration to probe alleged irregularities in special pass issuance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department will investigate allegations of irregularities in the issuance of special passes at the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office.
Its director, Datuk Hamsha Injau, said the department’s Integrity Division would conduct an investigation to determine the validity of the allegations and that no misconduct would be tolerated.
“Appropriate action will be taken if there is evidence of any breach of the law or regulations,” he said in a statement today.
He also advised the public to deal with the Immigration Department through official channels and avoid using unauthorised intermediaries.
A news portal reported today that special passes, which are intended to assist foreign nationals facing emergencies or urgent circumstances, were allegedly being systematically abused to extend their stay in Malaysia.
The report also alleged that the operation involved local intermediaries who handled applications, collected applicants’ passports and sent their photographs to immigration officers through messaging applications for preliminary verification. — Bernama

Title: N. Sembilan police: Post-mortem finds border agency officer died from pressure on neck, stab wounds
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 17 — Police said preliminary post-mortem findings showed that pressure applied to the neck caused the death of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer found at a government staff quarters in Nilai.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the finding followed a nearly five-hour post-mortem examination that began at 9.40 am today at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital here.
“The examination also found three stab wounds inflicted with a sharp weapon, two on the abdomen and one on the right cheek,” he said in a statement.
On October 15, the woman, who was in her 30s, was found dead at the quarters after she was believed to have been stabbed by her husband, reportedly following a misunderstanding.
Alzafny had earlier said police received a report about the incident at 9.30pm after the victim’s husband, also in his 30s, turned himself in at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported her death.
He was subsequently remanded until October 22 to assist in the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Army to review SOP after serviceman arrested with pistol, ammunition and ketum, says chief
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur.
Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army’s continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified.
“The same applies to this case. We are constantly monitoring. Although an SOP is already in place, we are always looking at continuous improvement,” he told reporters after the Passing Out Parade of Young Male Soldiers Series 206/26, involving 1,485 soldiers, here today.
The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.
Azhan said the individual, who is in his 30s, was undergoing a six-month transition training programme and was scheduled to complete his service in three months.
“For your information, the individual is undergoing transition training before completing his service and is currently detained at Sungai Buloh Prison for the trial process and further action,” he said.
He added that TDM would extend full cooperation to the authorities, including by providing the necessary information on the case.
Meanwhile, Malek Razak said the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) had its own procedures and investigation protocols for handling cases involving its personnel to ensure that all actions were taken in accordance with established regulations. — Bernama

Title: MAF reviewing allowances to boost reserve force participation, says Chief of Defence Force
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is reviewing allowances for its volunteer reserve personnel to encourage greater participation in training and strengthen the reserve force.
Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the review was aimed at boosting commitment among reserve force members and strengthening the manpower pool for the regular armed forces.
He said the current hourly rates of RM9.80 and RM8 were relatively low, having last been reviewed around 2022.
“We want them to participate actively in training and activities organised by their respective regiments. Active involvement also gives them additional points if they wish to join the regular force, making the screening process easier,” he told reporters after the passing-out parade for 1,485 recruits from the 206/26 Series of Male Young Soldiers Training here today. Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman was also present.
Malek Razak said an estimated 40 to 50 per cent of registered reserve personnel were inactive, including failing to attend training when called up.
Under existing policy, those who remain inactive for several months or years are removed from the membership list, he said, adding that this hindered efforts to maintain the Territorial Army as a reserve force.
“Our target is a one-to-one ratio between reserve personnel and regular armed forces personnel,” he said.
To improve participation, the MAF will diversify training methods, upgrade infrastructure and strengthen promotional efforts.
Malek Razak said graduates of the Reserve Officers Training Unit (PALAPES) were given priority to join the regular armed forces through the graduate officer recruitment scheme and could also receive additional academic credits.
“We believe it is a waste for them to undergo military training, particularly as officers, only to leave after completing their studies. We want them to become the next generation of officers in the regular service,” he said.
In a separate development, he said the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) would hand over some support assets to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) following the planned termination of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) mission early next year.
The assets include generators, general-purpose vehicles and other equipment that would not need to be returned to Malaysia.
Earlier, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said 292 assets worth an estimated US$10 million (about RM42 million) would be handed over in stages until January 2027 for welfare, humanitarian assistance and peacekeeping efforts for local communities.
Malek Razak also urged young people to join the MAF, particularly in technology, artificial intelligence (AI) and information technology (IT), to support the modernisation of the armed forces. — Bernama

Title: Home minister: Immigration depots facing capacity pressure amid daily enforcement operations
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — Immigration depots nationwide are facing capacity pressures due to daily enforcement operations against undocumented migrants, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said the depots had a combined capacity of about 20,000 people, but the continuous arrival of individuals detained during enforcement operations had led to overcrowding.
The increase in detainees is also result of the Immigration Department’s mapping of areas with high concentrations of foreign nationals based on data collected and analysed from enforcement operations nationwide.
“The mapping exercise enables the authorities to identify areas that are frequently used as settlements or gathering places by foreign nationals.
“Those detained may include individuals without travel documents, those holding expired passes, those who have misused their passes, or individuals with refugee status,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution was speaking at a press conference after attending the Home Ministry’s 2026 Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School launch ceremony here today.
He said action against each category had to take into account the individuals’ respective status and legal position, adding that enforcement operations also involved other enforcement agencies and local authorities.
Meanwhile, Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu had been identified as the four states recording drug-related case rates above the national threshold, based on figures per 100,000 population.
Saifuddin Nasution explained that the assessment was based on data from four sources, using a calculation method that referred to international standards.
Pendang in Kedah recorded the highest rate in the country, followed by Kuala Krai in second place.
Other districts identified were Tumpat, Tanah Merah and Bachok in Kelantan, as well as Besut in Terengganu, all of which recorded rates exceeding 1,000 cases per 100,000 population.
The data would be used to identify areas requiring more targeted prevention and enforcement measures, he said.
Saifuddin Nasution stressed that cooperation between the Home Ministry, National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK), police and state governments was crucial to intensifying awareness and prevention programmes in the affected areas.
These efforts would include community outreach programmes to educate the public and raise awareness of the dangers of drug abuse.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said about 75 per cent of the 90,000 inmates in prisons nationwide were involved in drug-related offences.
He said most of the inmates had been involved in offences under Sections 15(1) (self-administration), 12 (restriction on import and export of certain dangerous drugs) and 39 (general penalty) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
“Of the 41 prisons nationwide, Pengkalan Chepa Prison in Kota Bharu is among the most overcrowded.
“Based on the profile of prison inmates, those aged between 15 and 39 make up the largest group, while the involvement of children under 15 in drug-related cases is also a cause for concern,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution said the data also showed that unemployed people made up the largest group of those involved in drug abuse.
Commenting on patterns of drug abuse, he said synthetic drugs were more commonly linked to cases on the east coast, while drug use on the west coast involved a combination of synthetic and non-synthetic substances, adding that the use of synthetic drugs was particularly high because they were more readily available. — Bernama

Title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi from party activities for three months from Oct 20 after Jais incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Parti Bersama Malaysia has suspended Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months, effective October 20.
The party said the decision followed his public admission regarding his involvement in an incident with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) in Petaling Jaya on October 15.
In his earlier statement, Nik Nazmi
confirmed
he was the man caught with a woman, who is not his
muhrim
(a legally permissible close relative), in an enclosed space during the raid, and publicly apologised to his wife, family and party members.
“Bersama views this development seriously and takes the position that every issue involving the party’s leadership and members must be addressed appropriately to preserve the party’s integrity, credibility and public confidence,” Syukri Razab said in a statement on behalf of the party.
The suspension will run until January 19, 2027.
The party stated that the decision was necessary and reasonable, without denying Nik Nazmi’s contributions and commitment to Bersama since the party was relaunched in May 2026.

Title: Drug abuse among Malaysian under-15s a growing concern, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — The trend of drug abuse among those under the age of 15 is increasingly concerning and requires more comprehensive preventive efforts, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said that based on the profiles of individuals involved in drug abuse, those aged between 15 and 39 formed the largest group.
He added that this development necessitates a preventive approach that also emphasises early education and the role of parents in curbing the involvement of youngsters in drug abuse.
“The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) has three main functions, namely education and prevention, enforcement and rehabilitation, to address the issue of drug abuse.
“Efforts to educate the public must be strengthened to raise awareness and encourage preventive action among families,” he told a media conference after attending the Home Ministry’s Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School 2026 launching ceremony here today.
Meanwhile, commenting on the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos recently, Saifuddin Nasution said the drugs were found aboard the aircraft before it was due to depart for Manila.
He said the aircraft had departed from Subang for Laos without any drugs on board, before the consignment was loaded into the plane when it was in that country.
“Laotian authorities detected the drugs when the aircraft was about to continue its flight to Manila,.
“Police have traced the aircraft’s owner, as well as its pilot and co-pilot, to assist in the investigation as the aircraft had departed from Subang,” he said.
He said investigation was also focusing on the party that charted the aircraft, the purpose of the charter and its intended destination.
Saifuddin Nasution said the aircraft owner’s identity had been established, but further details of the investigation could not yet be disclosed.
Previously, Lao police seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 individuals arrested in connection with the case.
The Vientiane Times, quoting the Lao Security Newspaper, reported that the security operation was conducted on October 1 following information received by provincial police on Sept 21 regarding a drug trafficking syndicate believed to be planning to smuggle narcotics across the border by air, using a private aircraft.
According to the report, police subsequently received information about a change in the flight schedule, with the private jet expected to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30 pm on October 1. — Bernama

Title: Lawyer: Zara Qairina’s mother yet to decide on civil action as inquest nears conclusion
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — The legal team representing Noraidah Lamat, the mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, has yet to decide whether to pursue civil action against any party, with its immediate focus on completing written submissions for the inquest.
Counsel Shahlan Jufri, speaking on behalf of the team, said the matter would be discussed with Noraidah before any decision was made on further legal action.
“For now, our focus is on the inquest, particularly the written submissions. We will discuss the matter with our client, as the final decision on whether to take civil action against any party deemed responsible rests with her,” he told a press conference after the inquest proceedings yesterday.
Shahlan also revealed that Noraidah had sent a brief WhatsApp message that morning, expressing her hope that everything would be made easier.
He thanked members of the media for their coverage of the inquest, describing it as professional, accurate and timely.
Shahlan said the 96-day inquest had been a challenging process, although it had proceeded relatively swiftly alongside proceedings in the Court for Children.
“There is a lot that we need to address in our written submissions, and we hope the decision eventually reached will be fair to all parties,” he said.
On the funds raised to support the inquest, Shahlan clarified that the amount collected was slightly more than RM200,000, dismissing claims that it had reached RM1 million or RM2 million.
He said the fund was announced by Senator Marhamah Rosli last year and had been independently audited after Noraidah and the legal team appointed a qualified independent accountant in April this year.
According to Shahlan, the money was intended solely to cover expenses related to the inquest and had not been used for other purposes.
He added that the legal team had handled the case on a pro bono basis, meaning no legal fees were charged.
Shahlan also said there was no legal requirement for Noraidah or the legal team to make the audit report publicly available. — Daily Express

Title: Man loses RM363,887 in alleged fake bank auction property scam in Miri
Article:
MIRI, Oct 17 — A man who intended to buy a property for his family has allegedly been cheated out of RM363,887.49 in a non-existent bank auction property deal.
Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement shared on Miri police’s official social media page that the 56-year-old victim lodged a police report at Miri Central Police Station on October 15.
According to the police report, the victim had known the suspect for about two years through business dealings and friendship.
“In November 2025, the complainant intended to purchase a house for family use in Kuching. The suspect then allegedly offered five houses in the Taman Abadi area, Kuching, which were claimed to be bank auction houses at prices lower than the market rate.
“The suspect also offered to manage the purchase process, including the preparation of the Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and property title transfer,” said the statement.
Mohd Farhan said the complainant claimed to have made several payments in stages between November 2025 and January 2026 for the proposed purchases, including deposits, land surveying fees and payments related to the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN).
“However, the purchase arrangements were allegedly not completed as promised. The complainant also claimed that they have yet to receive complete documents proving ownership of the houses, despite contacting the suspect repeatedly for clarification,” he said.
Police are investigating the case under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property.
Police advised the public to be cautious of property offers at unrealistically low prices, verify property status through official channels, consult qualified lawyers and avoid transferring money to third-party accounts without proper verification. — The Borneo Post

Title: Transport minister: RM1,000 aid for remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers to be paid via EFT
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers nationwide will receive the RM1,000 Special Financial Aid directly into their respective bank accounts through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the disbursement through this method would be carried out in the next phase, following the first phase of direct handovers to eligible drivers in several zones.
He said that in the first phase, the aid would be handed directly to eligible recipients in selected zones, with Penang hosting the second presentation ceremony after the launch in Putrajaya on October 14.
“For the second ceremony, we are very pleased to be able to bring together 700 taxi and rental car drivers in Penang, who were selected as symbolic representatives to receive the aid in person.
“All the aid will be handed over to those who have been verified as eligible before Deepavali,” he told reporters after the special financial aid presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at Dewan Sri Pinang here today.
He also reminded drivers to ensure that they met the eligibility requirements to facilitate the screening of recipient data.
The main requirements include holding a driver card and a valid vehicle licence or permit (VP), as well as a valid Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licence.
Loke also urged drivers to keep abreast of announcements by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD), the Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) Sabah and LPKP Sarawak regarding the required information and verification process.
He said coordination among agencies under the Transport Ministry was important to ensure that the screening of recipient data was carried out transparently and fairly.
“I know that this RM1,000 may not solve all your problems or fully cover vehicle maintenance costs. However, I sincerely hope this assistance can, to some extent, ease your household expenses, help you replace worn-out tyres or fill your fuel tanks so that you can continue going out to earn a living,” he said.
On October 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced a one-off RM1,000 special financial aid for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers as one of the initiatives under Budget 2027. — Bernama
